_meta.purpose: Goal 1.4 — mine founder-email replies for theme/tone. For every reply Dave reports to a founder outreach email, Brad appends one entry here and tags it with ONE primary theme (optionally one secondary). After >=10 tagged replies, run the surfacing rule below to produce the top-3 themes, which feed (a) Tier 1.2 drip copy and (b) the next round of LinkedIn hooks.
_meta.howBradTags: When Dave reports a founder-email reply (pastes it, summarizes it, or says 'got a reply that said X'), Brad: (1) appends a reply object to `replies` with a new id `fer-YYYY-MM-DD-NN`; (2) sets `primaryTheme` to the single best-fit key from `themes`; (3) sets `secondaryTheme` only if a second theme is clearly present, else null; (4) captures a short `gist` (<=200 chars, Brad's paraphrase) and, when the reply has a vivid line worth reusing, a verbatim `quote`; (5) sets `sentiment` (positive|neutral|negative|mixed) and `examFocus` if known; (6) bumps `_meta.lastUpdatedAt` and `stats`. Never invent replies — only log what Dave actually reports.
_meta.surfacingRule: When `stats.total` >= 10, count `primaryTheme` occurrences (weight a `secondaryTheme` as 0.5). Output the top 3 themes with: count, one representative `quote`, the `dripImplication`, and the `hookImplication` from the `themes` map. Deliver as a short brief Dave can act on. Re-run each time total crosses a new multiple of 10.
downstreamConsumers: Tier 1.2 drip copy — the nurture email sequence; each top theme becomes an objection to preempt or a message to lead with.
Next-round LinkedIn hooks — each top theme becomes a candidate opener angle for draft-week-posts.

pricing-confusion.label: Confused / hesitant about pricing
pricing-confusion.definition: Asks what it costs, seems surprised by the price, compares to free tools, or misunderstands the trial (thinks a card is required, thinks $19 is per-exam, etc.).
pricing-confusion.dripImplication: Add a plain pricing-clarity beat to the drip: '$19/mo or $189/yr, 7-day trial, no card' stated once, cleanly.
pricing-confusion.hookImplication: A cost-of-failure hook (retake fee vs. one month of prep) reframes price without discounting.

loved-trap-framing.label: Loved the trap / 'why wrong answers look right' framing
loved-trap-framing.definition: Responds warmly to the metacognitive angle — the exam-lens / thinking-traps / 'the exam stops feeling like a trick' idea specifically.
loved-trap-framing.dripImplication: Lead the drip with the trap frame; it's the resonant hook — reinforce, don't bury it under features.
loved-trap-framing.hookImplication: Double down on concrete trap examples (one 4-option question, one plausible-but-wrong answer highlighted).

skeptical-of-ai.label: Skeptical it's more than a ChatGPT wrapper
skeptical-of-ai.definition: Questions whether the AI is real/useful, assumes it's generic LLM output, or worries about hallucinated explanations.
skeptical-of-ai.dripImplication: Add a proof beat: Bloom's classification + per-question trap detection, not free-form chat. Show, don't assert.
skeptical-of-ai.hookImplication: A 'here's the actual reasoning the AI gives' teardown hook counters the wrapper assumption.

cert-coverage-question.label: Asking if their specific cert is covered
cert-coverage-question.definition: Wants to know if PMP / Security+ / SHRM-CP / ITIL / CISSP / etc. is available or on the roadmap.
cert-coverage-question.dripImplication: Segment the drip by cert; surface the covered-cert list early and a 'request your cert' path.
cert-coverage-question.hookImplication: Cert-specific domain-weight hooks (proven Week 1 winner) for the certs prospects keep asking about.

credibility-question.label: Who are you / why should I trust this
credibility-question.definition: Asks about the founder, the company, track record, or wants social proof before trying.
credibility-question.dripImplication: Add the founder-story + credibility beat (real person, the Kopko PMI AI Standards signal) to the drip.
credibility-question.hookImplication: A founder-voice origin hook ('I built this because...') leans into the trust gap competitors can't match.

trial-friction.label: Signup / onboarding friction
trial-friction.definition: Tried but got stuck, confused about how to start, which exam to pick, or how the trial works mechanically.
trial-friction.dripImplication: Add a 'first 10 minutes' walkthrough beat; reduce activation friction directly in the sequence.
trial-friction.hookImplication: Not a hook driver — this is a product/onboarding signal to route to Dave, not a post angle.

timing-objection.label: Not in market / already passed / studying later
timing-objection.definition: Interested but timing is off — exam already taken, not scheduled yet, or on hold.
timing-objection.dripImplication: Long-cycle nurture branch: keep-warm cadence, 'when you're ready' framing, no hard CTA.
timing-objection.hookImplication: Low hook value; possibly a 'start before you schedule' reframe if this theme is large.

positive-generic.label: Positive but non-specific
positive-generic.definition: Warm reply with no particular objection or hook resonance ('looks great', 'nice, will check it out').
positive-generic.dripImplication: Weak signal for copy; treat as a soft-yes to move toward a trial CTA.
positive-generic.hookImplication: None — carries no directional information for hooks.

other.label: Other / doesn't fit
other.definition: Use sparingly. If 'other' becomes a top-3 theme, that's a signal to add a new theme key here.
other.dripImplication: Review the clustered 'other' replies and define a new theme.
